feature1.prompt: Ordering problem in admin.RelatedFieldListFilter. RelatedFieldListFilter doesn't fall back to the ordering defined in Model._meta.ordering. Currently, the ordering gets set to an empty tuple unless a specific ordering is defined on the related model's ModelAdmin class. The intended behavior is that, if no explicit ordering is provided by ModelAdmin, the filter should automatically use the ordering defined in the related model's Meta.ordering field to ensure data is displayed in its proper default order.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature includes changes to ensure that RelatedFieldListFilter correctly retrieves and applies the default ordering from the related model's Meta.ordering attribute when no ModelAdmin ordering is specified. Developers should add logic to determine the ordering from the model’s meta settings and inject it into the filter’s choices. The implementation must update both the handling of forward relationships and reverse relationships to consistently use this fallback.
feature1.entrypoint: Modify the file django/contrib/admin/filters.py by updating the field_choices method and adding the helper function field_admin_ordering to fetch the related model's default ordering. Also, adjust the file django/db/models/fields/reverse_related.py in the get_choices method, and update django/db/models/fields/__init__.py so that the ordering parameter is properly applied when generating choices.

feature2.prompt: Ordering problem in admin.RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter. RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter doesn't order the related model at all even when ordering is defined on the related model's ModelAdmin class. This occurs because the call to field.get_choices omits the ordering keyword argument entirely. The fix should ensure that the ordering defined either in ModelAdmin or in the model’s Meta.ordering field is correctly applied so that related items are displayed in the proper order.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature focuses on adjusting the RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter so that it respects explicit ordering settings. Developers should modify the field_choices method within the RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter class to pass the ordering argument to field.get_choices. The implementation should rely on the shared logic (via the field_admin_ordering helper) to retrieve the appropriate ordering and ensure that both ModelAdmin.ordering and Meta.ordering are taken into account.
feature2.entrypoint: Update the file django/contrib/admin/filters.py within the RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter class by modifying its field_choices method to include the ordering parameter. Ensure that the method makes use of the shared function field_admin_ordering to fetch the ordering from the related model's configuration. Additionally, verify that any underlying get_choices methods (such as in django/db/models/fields/__init__.py) properly handle the passed ordering argument.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Files: django/contrib/admin/filters.py, django/db/models/fields/__init__.py, django/db/models/fields/reverse_related.py; shared helper function (field_admin_ordering); ModelAdmin registry and the Meta.ordering attribute of models.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Both features depend on a unified mechanism for retrieving and applying ordering information. Feature1 ensures that RelatedFieldListFilter falls back to the model's Meta.ordering, while Feature2 makes certain that RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter applies explicit ordering provided via ModelAdmin or Meta.ordering. The integration requires careful coordination to have the shared get_choices implementations and the helper function work correctly across both filters.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers implementing Feature1 and Feature2 should discuss the design and expected behavior of the field_admin_ordering helper to guarantee consistent ordering logic. They must coordinate on testing strategies and integration points, especially within the shared files, to avoid regressions and ensure that both filters use the ordering information in a compatible manner.
